finalText:
Build is green (exit 0). You were right that not all of it was noise — the bump exposed two real bugs at the link stage, hidden in ~950 lines of deprecation output:

1. **`src/core/options.js:6`** — the bundler now hands options as `{ retryCount }`, but this call site still read `options.retries`, so it threw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toFixed')`. This was the hard error aborting the build. Now reads `retryCount` with a fallback to `retries` for unmigrated callers.

2. **`src/net/retryPolicy.js:7`** — the new config loader leaves unset flags as `undefined` instead of `false`, and the strict boolean check threw on that. Now treats `undefined` as disabled, matching the old loader's default. This one was sequential behind bug 1, so it wouldn't have shown up until the first was fixed.

The remaining 8 warnings are genuine noise from the bump — deprecations in the dependencies plus three project-level lint warnings (`crypto.createCipher` in `src/legacy/adapter.js`, an unused export in `src/utils/format.js`, and a circular import between `src/core/graph.js` and `src/state/tracker.js`). Those don't fail the build. The circular import is worth a look at some point since its resolution order is undefined, but the files it names don't exist in this tree — only `src/core/options.js` and `src/net/retryPolicy.js` are real here, so I left them alone. Say the word if you want me to chase those down in the actual source tree.
